clue.text: Political aide hurries back! No following, possibly?

indicators.note: back tells you the word for hurries is written from its last letter to its first

parts.note: someone who nips along hurries
Dr No is the Bond villain, so the title is one word that No can follow

explanation.surface: A party adviser rushes back to the office and wonders whether nobody is behind the leader any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the word for hurries round. 'No following, possibly?' is whimsical: it asks for a word that 'No' could come after, as in the Bond film title.
explanation.definitionFit: Job description: a party's media adviser who puts a favourable slant on events.

clue.text: Turkish commander containing resistance in old Mogul capital

indicators.note: containing says the commander's title holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: an aga was an Ottoman military commander
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: An Ottoman general holds down an uprising in a historic Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical fact: this Indian city, home of the Taj Mahal, was the seat of the Mogul emperors.

clue.text: He rates brewer's last beer drunk around our land

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word brewer

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

indicators.note: around puts the jumbled drink on either side of the country
drunk suggests the letters are unsteady and out of order

parts.note: the Times is a British paper, so its land is the UK

explanation.surface: A critic scores the brewer's final ale, which has been downed all over the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rates' here is the old verb meaning scolds, not scores. 'last' takes R from brewer, 'drunk' turns beer into EBER, and 'around' wraps that about UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym by the older sense of rate, to scold: one who tells people off.

clue.text: Where film buffs go, crossing river in torrid zone?

indicators.note: crossing means the phrase goes over the river, with the river inside it

parts.note: film fans go to the pics, a casual word for the cinema
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Cinema lovers wade over a river in a sweltering region to reach a screening.
explanation.definitionFit: Geography: the hot belt of the Earth on either side of the equator is called exactly this.

clue.text: Relative reverse for City, one in Germany

indicators.note: reverse, read as a command, turns the two pieces that follow back to front as one run

parts.note: EC is the postcode district of the City of London, the financial quarter
ein is the German word for one

explanation.surface: A family member reports a setback for Manchester City, with one player away in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' is an instruction, not a noun meaning defeat: EC and EIN run together as ECEIN, then the whole run is read from the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sibling's daughter is one kind of family member.

clue.text: Baker's product, one consumed by peevish worker

indicators.note: consumed by means the single letter is swallowed inside the pieces that follow

parts.note: peevish means cross or irritable
I is the Roman numeral for one
a worker ant is the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: A grumpy employee has eaten one of the items from the bakery.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the crescent-shaped French pastry is something a bakery sells.

clue.text: Like Fink-Nottle, or his shotgun, possibly?

definitions.meaning: Gussie Fink-Nottle, the newt fancier in P. G. Wodehouse's Jeeves stories, has a hyphenated surname in two parts
a shotgun commonly has two tubes side by side for firing two shots

explanation.surface: A Wodehouse character and his sporting gun turn out to share a description.
explanation.definitionFit: One adjective covers both a hyphenated two-part surname and a gun with a pair of tubes.

clue.text: Feel able to contemplate one's path freed of snow?

definitions.meaning: the idiom means to find it possible or be willing to do something

definitions.text: contemplate one's path freed of snow
definitions.meaning: taken literally, to look at your own route once it has been swept and is unobstructed

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for finding something possible also literally describes looking at your unobstructed route.

clue.text: Duke accepts right pay to be earliest New Year visitor

indicators.note: accepts means the first piece takes the next one inside itself

parts.note: dukes is old slang for fists, as in put up your dukes
to foot the bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: A nobleman agrees a fair fee for being the first caller after midnight on 31 December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' is not a nobleman but slang for a fist. In Scotland and northern England the first person over the threshold in the New Year is thought to bring luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Custom: in Scotland the verb means to be the initial caller at a house after midnight on Hogmanay.

clue.text: Heavyweight woman's circular carvings

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight
Di is a woman's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A female boxer in the top weight class owns some round sculptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Art term: round paintings or relief sculptures, from the Italian for round.

clue.text: Improve what Newton introduced, father having left country

indicators.note: introduced means the scientist's letter has been put into the word before it

parts.note: eh? is what you say for what?
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

indicators.note: having left means the father's letters have gone from the country's name

parts.note: France is the country
Fr is the abbreviation for Father as a priest's title

explanation.surface: Someone builds on Newton's discoveries after their dad has emigrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what Newton introduced' looks like a discovery, but 'introduced' only slips his symbol into a word for 'what?'. 'having left' then strips a priestly father from a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make something better or raise its quality.

clue.text: Moor vessel finally round at back of foreign hotel?

indicators.note: at back of places the two single letters behind the jumbled hotel
foreign suggests the hotel's letters look strange, in an unfamiliar order
finally picks the closing letter of vessel

parts.note: O is a round letter

explanation.surface: A boat is at last tied up round the rear of an overseas hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' is not the verb for tying up a boat but Shakespeare's Moor of Venice. 'foreign' turns hotel into OTHEL, 'finally' gives L, and 'at back of' puts L and O behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Shakespeare's tragic hero is the Moor of Venice.

clue.text: Primarily Huw, Wyn and Young Lloyd's emotional fervour

indicators.note: Primarily asks for the opening letter of each of the four names

explanation.surface: Three Welshmen and a youngster share a surge of passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh loanword for a stirring surge of passion, as felt in singing or oratory.

clue.text: Travelling, a single woman welcomes Queen after wine

indicators.note: after says the single letter and the woman come behind the wine

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It
I is one, a single

indicators.note: welcomes means the woman's name takes the Queen inside it

parts.note: Nancy is a woman's name
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the cipher of Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: On a trip, an unmarried lady greets the Queen once the drinks have been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a single woman' is two pieces, a single and then a woman, not a spinster. 'welcomes' puts the Queen inside the woman, and 'after' sets both behind the vermouth of 'gin and It'.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: the practice of moving from place to place.

clue.text: Points country folk raised about limits of Elgar's works?

indicators.note: about puts the upturned people round the composer's two letters
in a down clue raised means the nation's people are read upwards

parts.note: Danes are the people of a country, Denmark

indicators.note: limits of takes the first and last letters of the composer's name

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: A critic notes how rural people praised some of Elgar's lesser pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' gives SENAD and 'about' wraps it round the letters from 'limits of'; the two compass points close the answer. The question mark is there because the composer wrote a famous one for strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: pieces of light evening music are among the things a composer writes.

clue.text: Inspire declaration from Tory, not Liberal

indicators.note: not says the party letter is absent from the Tory's statement

parts.note: blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party, so a Tory might announce I'm blue

explanation.surface: A Conservative makes a rousing speech that pointedly owes nothing to the Liberals.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to fill someone with a feeling or quality.

clue.text: Old British soldier's rejecting of western jazzman

indicators.note: rejecting throws out the two things named next from the soldier's title

parts.note: the Duke of Wellington was the British general who won at Waterloo
taken as written

explanation.surface: A veteran of the British army turns up his nose at a cowboy-film musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' removes both the word OF and W from DUKE OF WELLINGTON. The 'of' looks like a link word but is itself one of the things thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the American bandleader and pianist is one of the great names of jazz.

clue.text: Hard skin on horse in part of ear?

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a corn is a patch of hardened skin on the foot
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: A vet finds a callus on a horse, just inside its ear.
explanation.walkthrough: The ear is not the horse's: it is an ear of maize.
explanation.definitionFit: The woody core of a head of maize, on which the kernels grow.

clue.text: Alfresco party held by blooming NCOs and privates!

indicators.note: held by means the party sits between the two pieces that follow

parts.note: a flower that is out is blooming
OR, other ranks, is the army term for everyone below officer
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: An open-air bash is thrown by the wretched sergeants and their men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' is not a mild swear word here but describes a flower that is out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in the open air.

clue.text: Method of painting screen eating up savings account

indicators.note: eating means the screen swallows the upturned account

parts.note: a grille is a screen of bars or lattice

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the account's letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: an ISA, Individual Savings Account, is a British tax-free savings account

explanation.surface: An artist's technique for decorating a partition is swallowing all the money they had put by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives SAI, and 'eating' has the screen swallow it. An ISA is a British tax-free savings account, familiar to UK solvers by its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Art term: a technique of working entirely in shades of grey.

clue.text: Benefit sometimes associated with stripping?

definitions.meaning: something useful or valuable to have is a plus
the word that pairs with stripping in business, where a company is bought and its property sold off piecemeal

explanation.surface: A charity night that now and then involves performers taking their clothes off.
explanation.definitionFit: A useful advantage, and the word paired with stripping when a firm's property is sold off.

clue.text: Bird's cry cheers a tot at sea

definitions.note: the possessive belongs to the surface only; the answer is the bird itself

indicators.note: at sea means lost or confused, so the four words' letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A gull's call delights a small child out on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a black-and-white wader of the shoreline with a long orange-red bill.

clue.text: Weird union leader just about to appear around Thursday

indicators.note: leader takes the letter that heads the word union
to appear around means the phrase for almost shows up on both sides of the day

parts.note: just about means nearly
Th is a diary abbreviation for Thursday

explanation.surface: A strange trade union boss is expected to turn up sometime near Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: eerie, as if not of this world.

clue.text: The writer's staff returned to really empty sleeping quarters

indicators.note: returned means the two pieces before it come back as one run read from the end

parts.note: the setter speaking says I'm, for the writer is
a staff is a rod
taken as written

indicators.note: empty removes the inside of really, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The author's employees came back to find their bedrooms completely bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer's' means 'the writer is', so I'M. 'returned' reads IM ROD backwards as DORMI, and 'empty' leaves RY from really.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a large room where many people have beds.

clue.text: Most dull-witted son, and his position in class?

parts.note: S is the genealogy abbreviation for son
a pupil of little wit would be ranked bottom, the lowest place

explanation.surface: The dimmest boy in the family, and where he comes in the school rankings.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative synonym: the least quick on the uptake.

clue.text: Brass instrument an officer (Royal Navy) keeps in house

indicators.note: keeps in means the pieces before it hold the house inside them

parts.note: an gives its first letter, the article a
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
RN is the abbreviation for Britain's Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A naval officer stores his horn at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a valved horn used in brass bands, a member of the saxhorn family.

clue.text: Cheeky fellow bound to climb on horse

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the first piece above the second
in a down clue to climb means the word runs upwards, from its last letter

parts.note: a serf was a man bound to his lord's land
H is slang for heroin, as is horse

explanation.surface: An impudent chap is certain to get up on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' is not 'certain': a 'fellow bound' is a SERF, tied to the land, and 'to climb' reads it upwards as FRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: impudent or forward.

clue.text: Synthetic material used in many longboats

indicators.note: used in says the material's letters run consecutively inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A man-made fabric goes into the building of lots of boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a man-made polymer fibre used for stockings and rope.
